yoda: Allow extensions for generated bash completions

When an option accepts string/int argument w/o choices,
make it possible for the user to provice "ycomp_<name>_<options>"
function that will be called to generate possible completions
for an option.

E.g. for

option	foo
	string	foo option

int a project named "bar" a function named "ycomp_bar_foo"
will be called when user types

$ name --foo <TAB>

yoda: Introduce (rather stupid) bash completion generation

Generation logic is like below:

1. If prev is ano option with argument -- complete argument
2. Scan current cmdline, properly skipping opts with args, for
   argument that switches options array, and report _this_
   arg array and gen options
3. If nothing of above met -- report switching-arg choices
   and generic options.

Wrong? Most likely yes, but works for typical usages of existing
examples/ tools.

yoda: Make one option assignment auto-assign something else to others

The "imply <expr>" line for an option (not argument) will lead to every
assignment to the option in question will lead to assigning smth to
other(s) specified by <expr>.

E.g.

option foo
 string foo string

option bar
 bool
 imply foo = foobar

For boolean targets '= value' part may be omitted.

(plan: make 'imply foo = $bar' or smth similar to work)

yoda: Swich options array

All options are groupped based on their for and req_for keywords.
Based on these groups option arrays (sets) are formed. When an
action on which options depend happens, the currently scanned array
is switched to new one and new set of options apply.

Options that do not have for/req_for fields are parsed in every
array.

yoda: Classify options for opt vectors switch

We'll be in situations when we'd have to scan for more than one
options array depending on current parse status.

The plan is to switch arrays based on 'req_for'-s and 'for'-s.
This patch generates options groups. Each group matches some
expression (currently -- only a single argument match) and
is about to switch options array.

yoda: Parse arguments in-order, rather than at the end of getopt loop

There are some scenarios (vzctl) when we need to keep track of arguments
in the argv[] array, rather than letting them all permutate to the end
of it and handle them later.

Now yoda generates parser, that scans argv-s one by one, assigning args
(if any) in-order, and after assignment of the last declared arg -- switch
the getopt_long to permutating mode.

yoda: Support for "pile"-d options

If an option is specified several times, then yoda will
report (in yopts structure) only the last value given.

Options with an attribute "pile" (it can be "set" and "unset")
collect all occurences of on option in the array. The number
of elements is given in the "<option>_nr" variable on yopts
structure.
